title: NBA Shot Selection Analysis
text:
This project provides a comprehensive analysis of NBA shot selection trends over 15 years (2010–2024). We scrape shot-level data using the nba_api, clean and process it, and analyze how teams’ offensive strategies have evolved, particularly their adoption of three-point shooting.
Explore the interactive dashboard: Streamlit App

title: NBA Shot Selection Analysis
text:
This project provides a comprehensive analysis of NBA shot selection trends over 15 years (2010–2024). We scrape shot-level data using the nba_api, clean and process it, and analyze how teams’ offensive strategies have evolved, particularly their adoption of three-point shooting.
Explore the interactive dashboard: Streamlit App

title: NBA Shot Selection Analysis
text:
Key Features

Automated data collection – Fetches shot-level data from NBA Stats API for all teams and seasons
Data cleaning pipeline – Standardizes zones, labels eras, handles edge cases
Trend analysis – Tracks league-wide three-point rate changes over time
Team rankings – Identifies early adopters and laggards in three-point shooting
Statistical analysis – Correlates three-point adoption with team success
Interactive visualization – Court heatmaps, time series plots, and comparative charts
Reproducible workflow – Full pipeline from raw data to insights

title: NBA Shot Selection Analysis
text:
Research Questions

How has the league-wide three-point rate changed from 2010 to 2024?
Which teams have been early adopters of three-point shooting?
Is there a correlation between three-point adoption and team wins?
How have shot zones evolved in usage over the 15-year period?

title: Technical Report
text: This technical report documents the methodology and architecture of the NBA Shot Selection Analysis project. It provides an overview of how we collect, clean, and analyze 15 years of NBA shot data to understand trends in three-point shooting adoption.

title: Technical Report
text: This technical report documents the methodology and architecture of the NBA Shot Selection Analysis project. It provides an overview of how we collect, clean, and analyze 15 years of NBA shot data to understand trends in three-point shooting adoption.

title: Technical Report
text:
1. Data Extraction
We use the NBA Stats API to collect official NBA statistics. The API provides shot-level data from the official NBA.com database.
Key endpoints used: - shotchartdetail.ShotChartDetail() – Individual shot attempts with coordinates and outcome - leaguedashteamstats.LeagueDashTeamStats() – Team-level offensive metrics
Data collection parameters: - Time period: 2010–2011 through 2023–2024 (14 seasons) - Teams: All 30 NBA teams - Season type: Regular season only - Context measure: Field goal attempts (FGA)

title: Technical Report
text:
2. Data Structure

Shot-Level Data
Each shot record includes: - TEAM_NAME – NBA team name - SEASON_1 – Season year - SHOT_ZONE_BASIC – Basic zone classification (e.g., “3PT Line”, “Paint”) - SHOT_ZONE_AREA – Detailed zone area - SHOT_DISTANCE – Distance in feet - LOC_X, LOC_Y – Court coordinates - SHOT_ATTEMPTED_FLAG – Whether the shot was attempted - SHOT_MADE_FLAG – Whether the shot was made (1) or missed (0) - SHOT_TYPE – “2PT Field Goal” or “3PT Field Goal” - ACTION_TYPE – Type of action (e.g., layup, jump shot)


Team Metrics Data
Team-season level aggregations: - TEAM_NAME – Team name - season – Season identifier - WINS – Regular season wins - OFF_RATING – Offensive rating (points per 100 possessions) - EFG_PCT – Effective field goal percentage - PACE – Possessions per game

title: Technical Report
text:
3. Cleaning and Standardization
Raw API data undergoes several cleaning steps:

Column standardization – Select and rename relevant columns
Data type conversion – Ensure numeric columns are properly typed
Zone classification – Standardize shot zone labels
Era labeling – Classify shots into “early” (2010-2014), “mid” (2015-2018), and “modern” (2019-2024) eras
Outlier handling – Remove incomplete or suspicious records
Team name matching – Ensure consistency across datasets

title: Technical Report
text:
4. Persisting the Output
Cleaned datasets are saved as CSV files for downstream analysis:
save_dataset(cleaned_shots, "data/shot_data_clean.csv")
save_dataset(cleaned_metrics, "data/team_metrics_clean.csv")
Both local and CI/CD pipelines ensure data is always in sync.

title: Technical Report
text:
5. Exploration Workflow
The analysis pipeline consists of:

Data loading – Read cleaned CSV files
Aggregation – Group shots by team, season, and zone
Metric calculation – Compute three-point rates, adoption rankings, correlations
Visualization – Generate court heatmaps, trend lines, and comparative charts
Export – Save results for reporting

All code is modular and reproducible using Python and standard data science libraries (pandas, matplotlib, plotly).

title: Technical Report
text:
6. Reproducibility Notes

Python version: 3.11+
Key dependencies: nba_api, pandas, matplotlib, plotly, streamlit, quarto
Data sources: Official NBA Stats API (no paid licenses required)
Runtime: Data collection takes ~5-10 minutes for full 14-season history depending on API rate limits

To reproduce:
uv sync
python src/data_collection.py
python src/data_cleaning.py
python src/analysis.py
streamlit run app.py

title: Technical Report
text:
7. Summary
This project demonstrates a complete data pipeline: from external API collection, through cleaning and standardization, to exploratory analysis and interactive visualization. The methodology is transparent, code is version-controlled, and results are reproducible on any machine with Python and internet access.

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.data_collection
Functions for fetching and saving NBA shot data from the official NBA Stats API.

get_shot_data(team_name, season)
Fetch shot chart data for a single team and season.
Parameters: - team_name (str): Team name, e.g., "Houston Rockets" or "Lakers" - season (str): Season in format YYYY-YY, e.g., "2018-19"
Returns: - DataFrame with shot-level data (coordinates, zones, outcomes)
Example:
from src.data_collection import get_shot_data
df = get_shot_data("Houston Rockets", "2018-19")
print(df.shape)


get_all_teams_shot_data(season, delay=0.6)
Fetch shot data for all 30 NBA teams in a given season.
Parameters: - season (str): Season in format YYYY-YY - delay (float): Seconds to wait between API calls (default: 0.6)
Returns: - Combined DataFrame for all teams
Example:
df = get_all_teams_shot_data("2018-19", delay=0.8)
print(f"Loaded {len(df)} shots")


get_multiple_seasons_shot_data(seasons, delay=0.6)
Fetch shot data across multiple seasons for all teams.
Parameters: - seasons (list): List of seasons, e.g., ["2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18"] - delay (float): Seconds between API calls
Returns: - Combined DataFrame across all seasons
Example:
seasons = ["2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18", "2018-19"]
df = get_multiple_seasons_shot_data(seasons)


get_team_season_metrics(season_range)
Fetch team-level offensive metrics for multiple seasons.
Parameters: - season_range (list): List of seasons
Returns: - DataFrame with one row per team per season (wins, offensive rating, etc.)


save_dataset(data, path)
Save a DataFrame to CSV.
Parameters: - data (DataFrame): Data to save - path (str): File path, e.g., "data/shot_data.csv"
Note: Parent directories are created automatically if they don’t exist.


load_dataset(path)
Load a CSV file into a DataFrame.
Parameters: - path (str): File path
Returns: - Loaded DataFrame

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.data_cleaning
Functions for cleaning and preprocessing raw API data.

clean_shot_data(df)
Clean raw shot data: standardize columns, classify zones, label eras.
Parameters: - df (DataFrame): Raw shot data from API
Returns: - Cleaned DataFrame with standardized columns


clean_team_metrics(df)
Clean raw team metrics data.
Parameters: - df (DataFrame): Raw metrics data
Returns: - Cleaned DataFrame

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.analysis
Functions for statistical and exploratory analysis.

three_point_rate_by_season(shots)
Calculate league-wide three-point rate (3PA / total FGA) by season.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - Series with three-point rate indexed by season


rank_teams_by_three_point_adoption(shots)
Rank teams by their overall three-point adoption rate.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - DataFrame with teams ranked by 3P rate (highest to lowest)


biggest_zone_shifts(shots)
Identify which shot zones have changed most in usage over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data
Returns: - DataFrame showing zone usage shifts


correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins(shots, metrics)
Correlate team three-point rate with win percentage.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Cleaned shot data - metrics (DataFrame): Cleaned team metrics
Returns: - DataFrame with correlation analysis results

title: Documentation
text:
Module: src.visualization
Functions for creating interactive and static visualizations.

plot_court_heatmap(shots, team, season)
Generate a court heatmap for a specific team and season.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data - team (str): Team name - season (str): Season
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_three_point_trend(shots)
Plot league-wide three-point trend over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_zone_distribution_over_time(shots)
Stacked area chart showing zone usage changes over time.
Parameters: - shots (DataFrame): Shot data
Returns: - Matplotlib figure


plot_three_pt_vs_wins(corr_df)
Scatter plot correlating three-point rate with win percentage.
Parameters: - corr_df (DataFrame): Correlation data from correlate_three_pt_rate_with_wins()
Returns: - Matplotlib figure
